1	\section{Discussion and Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
2	
3	Controlled SFT injection reveals qualitatively different dose-response patterns across model families---not uniform inflation---with vulnerability concentrated in the 65--70\% MMLU baseline band in our five-family sample. DiD analysis finds no item-specific memorization on MMLU (MDES 1.2--2.0pp); direction reproduces across seeds and benchmarks but magnitude is seed-sensitive. Out-of-sample validation on LLaMA-3.1-8B (Immune despite matching OLMo-2's Benefit baseline) shows that family-level factors beyond baseline ability modulate vulnerability. Candidate mechanisms include differences in pre-training corpus coverage of benchmark-adjacent knowledge---which may determine whether SFT injection reinforces or disrupts existing representations---and the degree to which instruction tuning has already saturated benchmark-style reasoning. Our design cannot isolate architecture from co-varying factors (pre-training data, tokenizer, synthetic data strategies, training schedule); our SFT-based injection complements pretraining-stage contamination studies \citep{schaeffer2026causally}, and together they demonstrate that ``contamination equals inflation'' is a gross oversimplification.
